author: sjm41
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
PTN004271263 (PTHR11567)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel CG16890 (FBgn0028932)
Human FRA10AC1 (Q70Z53)

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**
erroneous propagation?

I don't see any/much evidence for annotating Dmel CG16890/Human FRA10AC1 with 'phosphatase activity' via this node.
Both belong to the InterPro IPR050645 Histidine Acid Phosphatase family, though I'm not sure that's diagnostic. In particular, these proteins seem to lack the active site found in other members of the family.  The human protein is not annotated to be a phosphatase in UniProt.

Could you review and see what you think?
title: PAINT issue: PTN004271263 (PTHR11567)

author: marcfeuermann
body:
I was the one who annotated this term at the root of this large family because it appears scattered throughout the tree: 
ACP4 (human), ACP2 (mouse and rat), ACP3 (human, mouse and rat), acp-2 (worm), Acph-1 (fly), PXYLP1 (human), ACP6 (human), appA (E. coli) and agp (E. coli).
PTN000170711 containing Dmel CG16890/Human FRA10AC1 was the only node having no experimental annotations. The MSA was not really hekpful. I've now blocked the annotation to this node.

author: sjm41
body: Thanks Marc, I appreciate this family is a difficult one to annotate!

author: marcfeuermann
body:
You are welcome Steven. I love these kind of "challenging" issues. It is by far more interesting then removing contributes_to annotations ;-)
I learn a lot about evolution, it is fantastic. And I have a little less pressure these last weeks of the year which allows me to spend more time to handle such requests.
